newsitem.title: USA: Dow jumps to intraday record on mild CPI.
newsitem.headline: Dow jumps to intraday record on mild CPI.

text.p: New evidence that consumer prices remain in check sparked a broad rally in stocks that pushed the Dow industrials to record territory Friday.
At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average soared 79.53 points, or 1.38 percent, to 5,851.47, smashing the record 5,796.1 intraday high set on May 23.
In the broader market, advancing issues beat declines 17-5 on heavy volume of 284 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq Composite index jumped 19.27 points, or 1.65 percent, to 1,185.08 as technology stocks awakened from their recent slumber.
The Labour Department reported that consumer prices rose a mere 0.1 percent in August, helping the inflation-sensitive bond market to sharp gains, which carried over into stocks.
The benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond gained 1-21/32, sending its yield below the psychologically key 7 percent level to 6.94 percent from 7.08 percent at Thursday's close.
With the Dow finally able to establish a new high and technology stocks fully participating in the rally, analysts saw signs a new surge could be underway.

"Mood, momentum and money flow are back in gear," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co. "This is the magic moment that people have talked so often about, the Dow has broken through 5,800 and now some have lifted their sights to 6,000."
Technology stocks staged a particularly strong rally, sparked by votes of confidence from several investment firms.
SoundView Financial Group raised its recommended short-term weighting on the sector, saying it expected the group to outperform the broader market.

"We believe that over the next four to five months technology stocks as measured by the SoundView Index should outperform the broader averages on both a relative and absolute basis," SoundView's president and market strategist James Townsend said in a statement.
Industry bellwether International Business Machines Corp. jumped 4-3/4 to 122 after Merrill Lynch upgraded it to short-term strong buy with a 12-month target price of 150.

Other technology standouts included Intel Corp., up 2-1/2 to 87-7/8, and Microsoft Corp., up 1-9/16 to 130-3/16. Oracle Corp. surged 3-1/4 to 40-3/4 after Alex. Brown upgraded the shares to buy from neutral and Cowen & Co. reiterated its strong buy rating on the shares.
"Nasdaq had been lagging and for the moment it seems there's no reason to hold back," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd.

Many analysts have viewed the reluctance of investors to re-enter the technology and small-capital arenas as a critical obstacle to the continuation of a bull market that has lasted more than five years.
With market sentiment apparently improving, analysts are looking to indices like the technology-laden Nasdaq Composite for signs that there is steam left in the rally.
"When Nasdaq tests its old highs then we'll see where we really are," Bleier said.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 10.03 to 681.18. The American Stock Exchange index was up 4.21 to 570.87.
